acceptedAnswer.text: While general hardware adjustments are typically for functionality, certain installations must meet local building codes, such as those in Berkeley or Oakland, especially regarding safety and accessibility. For example, door hardware for egress paths or ADA-compliant fixtures must meet specific height, force, and operational requirements. While direct adjustments are not usually code-driven, ensuring the final functional state adheres to these regulations is crucial. Frasheski Construction is experienced with East Bay area codes, ensuring compliance from installation through final adjustments. This provides contextual relevance regarding local regulations.
